title: Game Genres — What Do You Like?
subtitle: Talk about game types, compare them, and share your preferences
description: Learn the names of popular game genres and how to compare them — using comparatives and preference phrases to talk about what you like and why.
heroImagePrompt: A young gamer sitting in front of a large screen split into four glowing panels — each showing a different game genre: action, horror, racing, and strategy — expression of excitement and choice, cinematic wide shot, dramatic colourful lighting
imageStyle: photorealistic cinematic still, movie trailer aesthetic, dramatic moody lighting, shallow depth of field, film grain texture, highly realistic people, high production value, widescreen composition, not stock photography

avatars.Alex: Close-up portrait headshot of a young male gamer named Alex, late teens, friendly confident smile, wearing a gaming headset around his neck, dark gaming room background with subtle RGB lighting
avatars.Sam: Close-up portrait headshot of a young female gamer named Sam, late teens, bright curious expression, casual style, dark gaming room background with subtle screen glow

grammarFocus.description: Use comparatives to say one thing is more or less than another. Use preference phrases to say what you like and why.
grammarFocus.positiveExample: "Action games are faster than puzzle games."
grammarFocus.negativeExample: "Horror games are more exciting than sports games."

positiveExamples.sentence: RPGs are longer than action games.
This game is harder than the last one.
Strategy is more difficult than racing.

negativeExamples.sentence: I prefer strategy to shooter games.
I'm not a big fan of horror.
negativeExamples.note: (polite way to say you don't like it)

vocabulary.definition: A category or type of game with its own style and rules.
vocabulary.example: What genre is this game? It looks like an action RPG.
vocabulary.imagePrompt: A large glowing game shelf showing many different game covers — action, horror, sports, puzzle — each glowing a different colour, dramatic cinematic lighting, wide shot

vocabulary.definition: A game type with fast movement, fighting, and quick reactions.
vocabulary.example: Action games are exciting — you fight and move all the time.
vocabulary.imagePrompt: A game character mid-combat, explosions behind them, dramatic motion blur, intense fighting pose, cinematic close-up, high energy

vocabulary.definition: A game type focused on exploring a world and following a story.
vocabulary.example: I love adventure games because the stories are amazing.
vocabulary.imagePrompt: A lone game character standing at the edge of a vast beautiful fantasy landscape, glowing horizon, cinematic wide shot, epic sense of exploration

vocabulary.definition: A game type where you plan your moves carefully to beat the enemy.
vocabulary.example: Strategy games are more difficult than action games — you have to think a lot.
vocabulary.imagePrompt: A glowing tactical map with military units and strategic markers, a hand hovering over it, dramatic blue lighting, cinematic top-down shot

vocabulary.definition: A game type designed to scare you with dark environments and scary enemies.
vocabulary.example: I don't like horror games — they are too scary for me at night!
vocabulary.imagePrompt: A gamer gripping their controller with a terrified expression, dark game screen showing a monster behind a door, jump-scare energy, dramatic horror lighting

vocabulary.definition: A game type where you drive vehicles and compete to finish first.
vocabulary.example: Racing games are faster than any other genre — the speed is incredible!
vocabulary.imagePrompt: A racing game cockpit view at extreme speed, motion blur on both sides, dramatic track lighting, intense velocity energy, cinematic close-up shot

vocabulary.definition: A game type where you solve problems and think creatively to progress.
vocabulary.example: Puzzle games are harder than they look — this level took me one hour!
vocabulary.imagePrompt: A satisfying puzzle piece clicking into place on a glowing game screen, colourful patterns, dramatic light when it fits, close-up cinematic shot

vocabulary.definition: A game type where you aim and shoot enemies to win.
vocabulary.example: Shooter games are more popular than strategy games in my group.
vocabulary.imagePrompt: A first-person shooter game perspective — weapon in foreground, enemy in crosshairs, dramatic cinematic lighting, intense focus and tension

vocabulary.definition: Making you feel energetic, happy, and very interested.
vocabulary.example: Action games are more exciting than puzzle games for me.
vocabulary.imagePrompt: A gamer leaping out of their chair in celebration, huge smile, screen behind them showing a victory moment, dramatic light and energy, cinematic wide shot

vocabulary.definition: Hard to do — needing a lot of skill and concentration.
vocabulary.example: This level is more difficult than the last one — I keep losing!
vocabulary.imagePrompt: A gamer staring intensely at a screen showing a very hard game level, frustrated but focused expression, dramatic close-up, determination in their eyes

vocabulary.definition: Liked and played by many people.
vocabulary.example: Battle royale is the most popular genre right now — everyone plays it.
vocabulary.imagePrompt: A massive esports arena filled with thousands of fans watching a battle royale match on giant screens, dramatic stadium lighting, crowd energy, cinematic wide shot

vocabulary.definition: To like one thing more than another.
vocabulary.example: I prefer adventure games to horror games — I don't like being scared!
vocabulary.imagePrompt: A gamer choosing between two game covers on a store shelf, one glowing brighter in their hand, dramatic choice moment, cinematic lighting

phrasalVerbs.phrase: what kind of games do you like
phrasalVerbs.definition: Ask someone about their favourite game type — a great conversation starter.
phrasalVerbs.example: What kind of games do you like? I love action and racing games!
phrasalVerbs.imagePrompt: Two gamers facing each other in a conversation, one gesturing to ask a question, friendly atmosphere, dark gaming room, cinematic medium shot

phrasalVerbs.definition: Use this to say you like one thing more than another.
phrasalVerbs.example: I prefer strategy games to action games — I like thinking carefully.
phrasalVerbs.imagePrompt: A gamer pointing confidently at their favourite game on screen, making a clear choice, dramatic lighting, cinematic shot

phrasalVerbs.definition: Use this comparative phrase to say one thing gives you more energy and interest.
phrasalVerbs.example: Action games are more exciting than puzzle games — they are so fast!
phrasalVerbs.imagePrompt: Two game screens side by side — one showing a calm puzzle, one showing an intense action fight, the action screen glowing brighter, cinematic comparison shot

phrasalVerbs.definition: Use this to tell someone which type of game you love the most.
phrasalVerbs.example: My favourite genre is RPG — I love the long stories and big worlds.
phrasalVerbs.imagePrompt: A gamer pointing to their chest proudly, RPG game world glowing on screen behind them, warm lighting, sense of pride and passion, cinematic medium shot

phrasalVerbs.phrase: i'm not a big fan of
phrasalVerbs.definition: A polite way to say you don't really enjoy something.
phrasalVerbs.example: I'm not a big fan of horror games — they are too scary for me!
phrasalVerbs.imagePrompt: A gamer gently pushing a horror game case away with a mild uncomfortable expression, polite refusal body language, soft lighting, cinematic close-up

phrasalVerbs.definition: Use this when something is more difficult than you expected.
phrasalVerbs.example: This puzzle game is harder than it looks — I cannot pass level 3!
phrasalVerbs.imagePrompt: A gamer with a surprised frustrated expression staring at what appeared to be a simple puzzle that turned out to be very hard, dramatic close-up, cinematic lighting

dialogue.speaker: Alex
dialogue.text: Hey Sam! What [[genre:a category of game]] of game are you playing? It looks intense!

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: It's an [[action:fast games with fighting and movement]] game! Action games are more [[exciting:making you feel energetic and interested]] than puzzle games for me. What do you [[prefer:to like one thing more than another]]?

dialogue.speaker: Alex
dialogue.text: I prefer [[strategy:games where you plan carefully to win]] games. They are more [[difficult:hard, needing skill and concentration]] than action games — but I love thinking carefully.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Really? I'm not a big fan of strategy. [[horror:games designed to scare you]] games are more [[popular:liked by many people]] than strategy in our group!

dialogue.speaker: Alex
dialogue.text: Ha! Horror games are scarier than strategy for sure. My favourite [[genre:a category of game]] is actually RPG.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: RPG? Those games are longer than other genres. Do you prefer solo or multiplayer RPGs?

dialogue.speaker: Alex
dialogue.text: Solo. Multiplayer is faster, but the story in solo games is better than in multiplayer.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: I understand! [[racing:games where you drive and compete at speed]] games are more fun than anything else for me — I love the speed!

dialogue.speaker: Alex
dialogue.text: Each to their own! What kind of games do you like most right now?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Racing! It is faster than any other genre and more exciting than watching real racing on TV!
